replies.stdout:
the verbs an agent on this computer reaches for, and the lines you type yourself:
up and down for the host, recipe and image for what a machine starts from.
  wsp computers set <computer> [--name <new>] [--ssh <login>] [--threads <n>]
    [--machines <n>] [--spend <usd>] [--size <cpu>x<memGb>]
    [--delete-after <minutes>] [--nap <minutes>|off] [--turn-limit <hours>|off]
    [--max-machines <n>] [--max-depth <n>] [--recipe <name>|none]
    [--reset <setting>]...
      what you set on one of your computers: its name, the ssh login it is
      reached by, how many threads run there at once, how long a quiet machine
      there runs before it naps, how long one turn there may run, the caps on
      agents starting agents, the recipe it follows, and on a cloud how many
      machines at once, how much it spends a day, the size a sub-thread's
      machine gets and how long a finished one stays; --reset takes a setting
      back to its default
  wsp recipes
      your saved recipes: what each puts on a computer in one line, and the
      computers that follow it
  wsp recipes show <name>
      one recipe whole: every row it holds by kind, the computers that follow
      it, and the hash it resolves to on this computer now
  wsp recipes save <name> --from <computer>
      saves what one of your computers was set up with as a recipe under that
      name, and that computer follows it from then on
  wsp recipes remove <name> [--yes]
      takes a recipe away; the computers that followed it keep what they have
      and follow none
  wsp usage [--range day|week|month]
    [--by agent|account|computer|project|model|source]
      what each agent account signed in on any of your computers may still use,
      and what was used over a day, a week or a month split one way, the work
      your agents logged outside wsp counted with wsp's threads as on the Usage
      page (--by source shows how much is outside); two answers, never added
      together
  wsp usage reset <account> [--credit <id>] [--on <computer>] [--yes]
      spends one of the resets a Codex account has banked, on a computer of
      yours that holds its login, after reading the account there: its five-hour
      and weekly windows start again now; asks first unless --yes
  wsp agents [<thread>] [--on <computer>]
      the coding agents on this computer, a box you added or where a thread
      runs: each one's version and the newest out, whether it is signed in
      there, and whether it carries the wsp tools
  wsp skills [<thread>] [--on <computer>]
      the skills on this computer, a box you added or where a thread runs, each
      by name with every folder it lives in and which agent loads it from there
  wsp skills search <query> [--limit <n>]
      searches skills.sh for skills by their words, each with how often it was
      installed and the id wsp skills add takes
  wsp skills show <skill> [<thread>] [--on <computer>] [--project [<name>]]
      prints a skill's SKILL.md: one on skills.sh by its <owner>/<repo>/<skill>
      before it is installed, or one already on this computer, a box you added
      or where a thread runs by its name
  wsp skills add <skill> [<thread>] [--on <computer>] [--agent <id>]...
    [--project [<name>]]
      installs a skill off skills.sh by its <owner>/<repo>/<skill> into the
      shared skills folder, with a link or a copy for each agent named that does
      not read that folder; every file is checked first and lands as a plain
      file that runs nothing
  wsp skills remove <name> [<thread>] [--on <computer>] [--project [<name>]]
    [--yes]
      removes a skill by its name: every folder it lives in and every link to
      it, where a link's own folder elsewhere stays
  wsp skills disable <name> [<thread>] [--on <computer>]
      turns a skill off by its name, its SKILL.md renamed SKILL.md.off where it
      lives, so no agent loads it until it is turned on
  wsp skills enable <name> [<thread>] [--on <computer>]
      turns a skill that was turned off on again, its SKILL.md.off renamed back
  wsp servers [<thread>] [--on <computer>]
      the MCP servers the agents on this computer, a box you added or where a
      thread runs are set up with: how each is reached, the file it is defined
      in and its sign-in as its config says it
  wsp agents signin <agent> [<thread>]
      signs an agent in on this computer or where a thread runs, its own sign-in
      run there and shown in this terminal; a box you added takes wsp add
      <computer> --sign-in <agent>
  wsp agents key <agent> [--api-key]
      puts an agent's token or API key into this host's vault, typed where
      nothing echoes it; Claude Code's token is the one claude setup-token
      prints, Codex signs in on this computer with its own login, which machines
      at a provider use through wsp, and --api-key takes the agent's API key
      instead
  wsp agents addtools <agent>
      writes the wsp server into an agent's own config on this computer, the
      entry wsp mcp install writes, with the wsp skill beside it
  wsp agents default <agent>
      the agent a new thread runs when neither the line nor its project names
      one; the catalog's first without it
  wsp agents set <agent> [--model <slug>] [--effort <word>] [--access <word>]
    [--hide <model>]... [--show <model>]... [--order <model,model>]
    [--add-model <id>]... [--drop-model <id>]... [--reset <field>]...
      an agent's defaults on every computer: the model, effort and access a new
      thread on it starts on, and which models its picker lists
  wsp agents setup <agent> [--on <computer>] [--enable | --disable]
    [--program <path>] [--config <folder>] [--arg <word>]... [--env <NAME>]...
    [--unset-env <NAME>]... [--reset <field>]...
      how an agent runs on one computer: on or off there, the program run in its
      place, its config folder, words added to every launch and variables every
      launch carries, each value typed where nothing echoes it
  wsp servers signin <name> --agent <id> [<thread>] [--on <computer>]
      signs one MCP server in by its agent's own command for it, run where the
      server is set up and shown in this terminal
  wsp servers tools <name> --agent <id> [<thread>] [--on <computer>]
    [--project <name>] [--refresh]
      starts one MCP server once where it is set up and lists its tools with
      their descriptions, and says whether it needs a sign-in
  wsp servers add <name> [<thread>] [--on <computer>] --agent <id> (--command
    "<line>" | --url <address> [--header <name>=<VARIABLE>]...)
    [--env <NAME>]... [--project [<name>]]
      writes one MCP server into an agent's own config: a command with its
      arguments and variables, or an address with its headers, each value read
      off this terminal's environment: the file names a variable and the value
      goes to the vault, an argument or the address naming a variable as ${NAME}
      keeps that name there, and an agent that reads no variable there refuses
      it
  wsp servers remove <name> [<thread>] [--on <computer>] --agent <id>
    [--scope <user|home|local|project>] [--project [<name>]] [--yes]
      takes one MCP server's entry out of an agent's own config, every other
      line of the file as it was, and, once no agent's config on this computer
      lists that server, frees the vault's values kept for it that no other
      server holds
  wsp servers disable <name> [<thread>] [--on <computer>] --agent <id>
    [--scope <user|home|local|project>] [--project [<name>]]
      turns one MCP server off by the switch its agent reads, so the agent
      leaves it out until it is turned on
  wsp servers enable <name> [<thread>] [--on <computer>] --agent <id>
    [--scope <user|home|local|project>] [--project [<name>]]
      turns an MCP server that was turned off on again
  wsp plugins [<thread>] [--on <computer>]
      each agent's plugins on this computer, a box you added or where a thread
      runs: on or off, missing where the agent names one it cannot load, its
      marketplace and version, and what it brings
  wsp plugins disable <id> --agent <id> [<thread>] [--on <computer>]
      turns one agent's plugin off for the login, by the agent's own road, so
      its next turn loads nothing of it
  wsp plugins enable <id> --agent <id> [<thread>] [--on <computer>]
      turns one agent's plugin that was turned off on again
  wsp projects remove <project> [--yes] [--force]
      takes a project out of this wsp; its folder is left where it is, on this
      computer or on a computer you joined, a project with a machine standing on
      it is refused naming them, and one whose checkout on a computer of yours
      holds work no remote has is stopped naming it
  wsp projects set <project> [--agent <id>] [--model <slug>] [--effort <word>]
    [--access <word>] [--after-worktree <command>] [--tracker <owner/name>]...
    [--reset <field>]...
      what a new thread on one project starts on, over the agent's own defaults:
      its agent, model, effort and access; the shell line a new worktree of it
      runs once, after each ecosystem's own install, for what none of them
      knows; and the repos besides its own that gh on a sub-thread's machine may
      comment on, the whole list each time
  wsp projects seed <project> [--keep <path>]... [--cut <path>]... [--none]
    [--yes]
      what git ignores in a project's folder on this computer, and which of it
      goes to a sub-thread's machine: the menu with each path's size and why,
      the picks marked; --yes saves the picks, which every later sub-thread of
      the project takes
  wsp threads wait <thread>... [--timeout <s>] [--tail]
      blocks until one of the threads leaves running and prints its finished
      line, with the reply whole under it; --tail prints the reply's last line
      alone, which is what a notify sends, and --timeout gives up after so many
      seconds and says so on stderr
  wsp commit <thread> [--message "<message>"] [--file <path>]...
      commits every changed file in the folder the thread works in, other
      threads' changes there included, or the files named; without a message the
      thread's agent drafts one
  wsp discard <thread> <path> [--yes]
      puts one changed file in the folder the thread works in back as its last
      commit has it, or removes it where that has none
  wsp fix <thread> [--check "<name>" | --child <thread>]
      asks the thread's agent to fix a failed check or merge a child, or updates
      its folder from its base and asks it to fix what conflicts
  wsp merge in <lead> <child>
      merges a child thread's branch into its lead's folder with a merge commit,
      or names the files that conflict
  wsp merge <thread> [--method merge|squash|rebase] [--when-checks-pass]
      merges the pull request of the thread's branch, or merges it once its
      checks pass
  wsp start <link> [--project <name>] [--agent <id>]
    [--model, --effort, --access <word>]
      a thread off a GitHub issue or pull request link, the issue or the pull
      request its first message; an issue's thread runs in the project folder, a
      pull request's in a worktree on its branch
  wsp review <link|thread> [--agent <id>] [--model, --effort <word>]
      a reviewer thread on a pull request, read-only, whose review waits in wsp
      until you post it
  wsp review post <thread> [--verdict comment|approve|request-changes]
    [--summary "<text>"]
      posts a reviewer thread's review on its pull request as you, its ticked
      comments on their lines
  wsp update <thread>
      merges the latest commits of the base into the branch of the folder the
      thread works in, or names the files that conflict
  wsp image
      the image this host owns: its version, its hash, whether it holds your
      sign-ins (an image built on Boat holds none), and the copy each place has
      built of it
  wsp image build <place> [--force]
      builds this host's image at a place from the record, its sign-ins coming
      from the vault and no sign-in run again
  wsp worktree <project> <branch>
      a worktree of the project's repo on the branch, for an agent to work in by
      path or to start a thread in: the one git already has the branch checked
      out in, wherever it is, else one wsp makes under its own folder, from the
      project folder's current commit for a new branch, with the folder's .env
      files and installed dependencies carried in; prints its path
  wsp worktree remove <project> <branch> [--force] [--yes]
      takes away a worktree wsp made for the branch, with git: refused while a
      thread is working in it, and over files no commit holds unless --force;
      the branch stays, and a worktree wsp did not make is never removed
  wsp thread read <thread> [--last]
      the thread's messages as the app lists them, oldest first: who each one
      is, when the runtime recorded it and the text, with every tool call folded
      to the one line the app's row reads; --last prints the final reply alone,
      the whole message its finished line carries. A tool's output and the
      agent's reasoning are no rows of it. Reading marks the thread read, so it
      stops reading Done here and in the app
  wsp thread head <thread>
      the thread's facts and its newest events, what the app draws first on
      opening it: the title, the agent, model and access it runs on, where it
      stands and its folder, then as many of its newest events as fit in 64 KB,
      each tool result past 2 KB cut and marked with its whole length. Reading a
      head marks nothing
  wsp thread forget <thread> [--yes]
      drops a thread no turn ever ran on, the row a launch that never got going
      leaves behind; refused once a turn of it did work
  wsp thread settle <thread>... [--finished] [--processes stop|keep]
      folds each thread and every thread under it into the sidebar's Settled,
      leaving a tree with a thread still working or asking in it; a thread
      settles itself and the threads it started, never its lead; refused while
      one still runs processes, on this computer or a box, unless --processes
      says to stop or keep them
  wsp thread restore <thread>...
      brings each thread back out of the sidebar's Settled with what the latest
      settle naming it moved
  wsp thread allow <thread>
      answers the prompt the thread is stopped on and lets the call run
  wsp thread deny <thread> [--reason "<words>"]
      answers the prompt the thread is stopped on and refuses the call
  wsp slate catalog [<name>]
      what a slate can hold: the index of pieces, sources, steps, functions and
      rules, or one entry in full
  wsp slate write [<thread>] [<file>] [--check] [--set <path>=<json>]...
    [--press <piece>] [--row <n>] [--action <n>] [--if-version <n>]
      writes the thread's slate from a .slate file (a whole <slate> or a patch)
      or a .json document and prints its sketch; --check stores nothing, and
      with --set or --press rehearses values and a press on a copy, the file
      optional
  wsp slate state [<thread>] [<path>=<json>...] [--start <run>]...
    [--if-version <n>]
      sets the slate's $values by path, like '$steps[2].done=true' or 'i=2',
      starts runs the person let run every time, and prints its sketch
  wsp slate read [<thread>] [--values <path>]... [--no-text] [--no-sketch]
    [--document]
      the slate as it stands: the sketch, then the JSX-like form, the values,
      derived values, runs, problems and the paths named; --no-text leaves out
      the JSX-like form, --document adds the stored JSON
  wsp slate look [<thread>] [--width <px>] [--out <file>]
      draws the thread's slate as the app's window does, in the person's theme
      at the panel's width, and saves it as a PNG; the tool answers the picture
  wsp restart
      stops the host and brings it back on the road it came up on, its service,
      the verb that started it or the app; running turns go on and the host that
      comes back re-opens them. A host wsp up holds in a terminal refuses
  wsp exec <thread> [--cwd <dir>] -- <command...>
      runs the command where the thread works, each word as given, in --cwd or
      the thread's own folder
  wsp conversations [<project>] [--agent <id>]
      the conversations Claude Code and Codex kept in the project's folder and
      its worktrees outside wsp, newest first, each with its id, last change,
      size, branch and title, and whether another app holds it open; wsp run
      --resume <id> opens a thread on one
  wsp activity [<thread>] [--computer <computer>] [--wide]
      this computer's processes, or a box's, as Settings > Activity lists them:
      wsp's own, then each thread heaviest first with what it started, then what
      has no thread, each with its kind, ports, memory and CPU; a thread named
      shows its own alone, on this computer or the box it runs on
  wsp activity end <pid> --started <ms> [--computer <computer>]
      ends one process on this computer and everything under it, by the pid and
      the start wsp activity --json listed: TERM, then KILL after 2 s; refuses a
      process wsp did not start, an agent, which wsp stop ends, and a pid that
      names another process now
  wsp mcp install --agent <id> [--agent <id>] [--host <alias>] [--json]
    [--remove]   (claude, codex, gemini, opencode)
      put the wsp tools, this skill and wsp's own section of this project's
      AGENTS.md into that agent (claude, codex, gemini, opencode); --agent
      repeats, --remove takes it back out, and --json prints what each agent
      took
  wsp up [--port <n>] [--listen <addr>] [--advertise <url>] [--no-relay]
    [--service]
      serve the host in this terminal, for a host you want to watch or one that
      serves beyond this computer; --service hands the same line to this
      computer's own service manager, which starts it now and again at every
      login. A line that needs a host starts one when none serves.
  wsp down
      stop the host: the service and its unit where one holds it up, and
      otherwise the host the command line brought up, whether wsp up or a verb
      that needed one started it
  wsp join <url>... --code <code> [--code-file <path>] [--name <name>]
      on the computer you are sitting at: join it to the wsp at that address,
      then install the daemon as a systemd system unit, which dials again at
      every boot. A place is a Linux computer; a Mac refuses
  wsp leave [--yes] [--force] [--takes <project folder>]...
      on that computer: take wsp off it, for a computer whose host is gone and
      cannot run wsp remove; asked once, and stopped by a fork or a project
      checkout there holding work no remote has, naming each

  wsp run and wsp send stream the reply as it arrives and print it once: on a
  terminal the streamed copy is the reply, and into a pipe stdout carries it whole
  at the end.
  A turn ends when the agent process exits, not at its reply, and the thread
  reads running until then.
  wsp exec streams the command's output and exits with its code. run, send and
  exec wake a paused machine first, with one line on stderr saying so.

every verb takes:
  --json         print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
                 everything else on stderr
  --state        the state file the host serves
  --host         run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
                 hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

exit codes; every failure is one line on stderr, the failure object with --json:
  0 ok        it did what its line says; with --json stdout holds the answer
  1 provider  the host, the runtime, a provider or the machine refused or failed
  2 auth      no key, no sign-in, or the host refused the token
  3 usage     the line was refused before anything ran: a missing argument, an
              unknown flag or a value nothing takes
